metadata.s6_2_disclosure:
S6.2  Mandatory disclosure block in the output (reviewer must-fixes carried forward):
        - the 15 no-op pairs by CATEGORY: numerical precision x8, head-only unembedding x3,
          system-prompt x2, DPO x1, rank-one lesion alpha 0.5 x1; re-saves EXCLUDED as trivially zero;
          ALL THREE LoRA ARMS FAILED TO BE NO-OPS.
        - the defensible 12-pair denominator (BL1_easy 4/12 vs N1 1/12), not only 6/15 vs 1/15.
        - SENSITIVITY IS THE BINDING FAILURE, NOT SPECIFICITY, and the trade-off runs THROUGH the
          activation class (C13_peak_d and N11 are the two most sensitive at 6/9 and the two least
          specific at 3/15 and 2/15), not along the activation-vs-logit boundary.
        - the BL1 variant ordering FLIP, disclosed in every table.
        - AMS at batch 1 AND batch 8 with the padding hazard named.
        - the two over-refusal measurements reconciled BY NAMING THE BENIGN SET IN THE COLUMN HEADER
          (XSTest twins 0.11 instruct / 0.00 SafeRL vs hard-benign probes 0.438 / 0.479).
        - PRIOR-ART FENCES: MUST NOT claim a first cross-family few-prompt activation metric (AMS);
          a first internal scoring of abliterated checkpoints; reference-free or <=16 prompts as
          novelty; recognition/execution naming; any weights-only statistic; a first decode-site
          readout (2609.18471); a first readout-under-quantisation or benign-fine-tune FPR (Duan
          2606.15980, Hurtado); a first logit-vs-activation comparison; a first random-direction
          control; or the read-vs-write dissociation itself (Basu 2603.18353, Galeone 2606.24952 own
          it at the model level; it is a PREMISE here). Self-repair and backup behaviour are
          established in the circuits literature; W4 is a SCALARISATION, never a discovery.
metadata.verdict: NO CANDIDATE PASSES THE REGISTERED BAR: 11 frozen survivors, 0 confirmed on clause (ii) [confirmation FULL, n=12, MDE=0.7321442233518527]. P1 (the one-coordinate bound) is ALSO NOT SUPPORTED (effective rank 7.16, |cos| with BL1_easy 0.645). THE DELIVERABLE IS THE MEASURED TRADE-OFF: on the blind panel the self-fitted ACTIVATION readouts predict over-refusal (|rho| 0.94 W3 n=6, 0.82 G4 n=12, 0.68 the difference-in-means FLOOR, 0.67 G3) where the final-layer LOGIT GAP does not (+0.15) and AMS sigma lands at +0.66 with the OPPOSITE sign; the five GEOMETRIC candidates (G1-G4, A3) and W2 raise ZERO false alarms on 24 behaviourally graded no-op edits where the logit gap raises 11 (exact McNemar p=0.00098; W2 0 vs 7 on its 14 evaluable pairs, p=0.0156) while W1 is LESS specific than the logit gap (6 vs 1, p=0.125) and W7 is 2 vs 1, and all of them detect at most 3/10 real safety-changing edits (G3 3, G1 2, G4 2, A3 1, W1/W2/W7 0); and every observed sign is OPPOSITE to the registered expectation, so these readouts locate a checkpoint on the refusal/permissiveness trade-off rather than measuring 'more safety'. Per-candidate: A2:not-confirmed-primary; A1:not-confirmed-primary; G4:not-confirmed-primary; W2:not-confirmed-primary; W3:not-confirmed-primary; W7:not-confirmed-primary; A3:not-confirmed-primary; W4:not-confirmed-primary; W1:not-confirmed-primary; G3:not-confirmed-primary; W5:not-confirmed-primary

commissioned_quartet_headlines.source: results/screen/quartet_tierA.json (array-only, iteration-2 harvest, 256-row frozen stimuli, prereg band rule)

headlines.claim: Abliteration ROTATES the request axis, and the rotation is near-total at mid-depth.
The abliterated child still separates harmful from hard-benign along ITS OWN axis, while the parent's axis has gone nearly blind on it - the direct argument for self-fitted, parent-free readouts.
headlines.numbers: At B4, Cohen's d of H vs P for the abliterated model: 4.83 along its own F, 0.22 along the instruct model's F. (B5: 4.47 vs 2.33; B6: 4.21 vs 3.12.)

headlines.claim: The official safety fine-tune does NOT move the axis; it sharpens the separation along it.
headlines.numbers: |cos(F_instruct, F_SafeRL)| = 0.997, 0.982, 0.916, 0.932, 0.926, 0.873 (>= 0.84 in every band, reproducing iteration 4); d(H vs P) at B4 = 6.63 (SafeRL) vs 5.78 (instruct); cross-projection at B4: SafeRL scores 6.38 along the instruct axis vs 6.63 along its own.

headlines.claim: Instruction tuning CREATES the axis: the base model's own harmful-vs-benign direction is different and much weaker.
headlines.numbers: |cos(F_Base, F_instruct)| = 0.527, 0.280, 0.167, 0.125, 0.091, 0.145; d(H vs P) at B4 = 1.95 (Base) vs 5.78 (instruct); |F|/mean residual norm at B4 = 0.133 (Base) vs 0.423 (instruct).

headlines.claim: A NON-safety fine-tune of the same base (CohenQu STaR) rotates the axis far less than abliteration does - rotation at B4 is not a generic fine-tuning artefact.
CONTRADICTS the plan's inherited claim that abliteration 'rotates but does not shrink': at the prompt site the abliterated 4B model both rotates AND loses ~40% of the axis magnitude.
headlines.numbers: |F| ratio (abliterated / instruct) per band = 0.933, 0.840, 0.864, 0.571, 0.578, 0.603; |F|/mean residual norm at B5 = 0.351 (abliterated) vs 0.589 (instruct). The iteration-4 figure (|N6| 1.79 vs 1.87) was a raw norm on a different item set and could not be reproduced from disk (see results/regression_check.json).

headlines.claim: The 'looks alarming' and 'is harmful' axes nearly coincide in the aligned chat models and separate in the base/control models (this is candidate G1's raw material).

commissioned_quartet_headlines.caveat: All five arms are > 2.2B parameters, so they are array-only here (no GPU intervention pass) and are EXCLUDED from the screen panel's correlation statistics by the prereg, exactly as registered.

per_item_array_coverage.note: 20 of 37 overwritten per-item .npz files were restored, all with registered_drift == {} (zero drift); the remaining files were not recoverable and their pairs/candidates are marked NOT_BOOTSTRAPPABLE (see metadata.selection_clauses.not_bootstrappable).

items: Activation-patching validation DISAGREES with the causal write-handle scalar (W1) in sign and magnitude across the three rows it was run on (F1__ref, F2__ref, and the Huihui-Qwen3-0.6B-abliterated-v2 arm): the per-item Spearman between the real activation patch and W1's project-out effect at B4 is approximately +0.53 on one row, -0.54 on a second, and +0.40 on the third -- i.e. it does not even agree in SIGN across rows, so W1 is not validated as tracking a real causal patch consistently.

W2 (the smallest-k ablation-ladder candidate) is fold-unstable: its greedy nested band order is fit separately per cross-fit fold and frequently disagrees between fold A and fold B, and its CENSORED sentinel value (7, for rows where no k in 1..5 reaches the 50% threshold) is averaged in with genuine small-k values when the registered value is taken as the mean of the two fold assignments -- so a single W2 number can mix a real ladder step from one fold with a censoring code from the other.

The W-family's normalising 'gap' (|mean_H<X[B6],r_late> - mean_P<X[B6],r_late>| on the scoring fold) is DEGENERATE (near zero) on at least two base models, pythia-410m and Pleias-1.2b, which makes every W-scalar on those rows numerically unstable (small-denominator blow-up) rather than a genuine large effect.

15 of the panel's Llama-3.2 / Qwen2.5 arms carry a RENDER_MISMATCH flag: the Tier-B capture's unperturbed last-token activations do not reproduce the iteration-4 stored A_prompt rows to within the 5e-2 tolerance. The likely cause is that Llama-3.2's chat template injects the CURRENT DATE into the rendered prompt, so re-rendering at Tier-B time (a different wall-clock date than the iteration-4 harvest) produces a token sequence that differs from the stored one.

6 of the panel's arms are LoRA/DPO fine-tunes for which no Tier-B (intervention-pass) row was built at all -- they carry Tier-A candidates only; every W-family value for those 6 arms is missing, not zero.
